chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, all together from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed Allah, the Exalted, revealed to ʿImrān: “I am granting you a sound, blessed male child who will cure the blind and the leper, and bring the dead to life by the permission of Allah, and I will make him a Messenger to the Children of Israel.”
So ʿImrān informed his wife Ḥannah of that, and she was the mother of Maryam. Then when she conceived, in her own mind she thought that her pregnancy was a boy.
Then when she gave birth to her, she said: “My Lord, indeed I have delivered a female.”
“And the male is not like the female” — meaning: a daughter would not be a Messenger.
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And Allah knew better what she had delivered.”

So when Allah, the Exalted, granted ʿĪsā to Maryam, he was the one about whom ʿImrān had been given glad tidings and promised. Thus, when we say something about a man from among us, and it comes to be in his son or the son of his son, then do not deny that.

key_terms.أَوْحَى: revealed; divine communication from Allah to ʿImrān
key_terms.أُنْثَى: a female; referring to the birth of Maryam
key_terms.بُشِّرَ: was given glad tidings; the promised good news to ʿImrān
key_terms.ذَكَرًا: a male child; the promised offspring mentioned in the revelation
key_terms.رَسُولًا: a Messenger; one sent by Allah to convey revelation
key_terms.وَلَدِهِ: his son/offspring; indicating fulfillment through descendants
key_terms.يُبْرِئُ: he cures; referring to miraculous healing

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain Allah’s promise to ʿImrān and its fulfillment through ʿĪsā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the divine promise given to ʿImrān was fulfilled through his descendant, namely ʿĪsā عليه السلام born to Maryam عليها السلام. It also comments on the Qur'anic account of Maryam’s birth and establishes a principle that a promise or designation concerning one person may be realized in his offspring or grandson.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Riab, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Revealed unto Imran<sup>as</sup>: “I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Grant to you<sup>as</sup> a male (son), perfect, Blessed. He<sup>as</sup> will cure the blindness and leprosy, and he<sup>as</sup> will revive the dead by the Permission of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and I<sup>azwj</sup> shall Make him<sup>as</sup> a Rasool<sup>as</sup> to the Children of Israel”.

So Imran<sup>as</sup> narrated it to his<sup>as</sup> wife Hanna with that, and she is the mother of Maryam<sup>as</sup>. So when she was expecting, it was so that within herself she thought it was a boy.
[3:36] So when she gave birth to it, she said: My Lord! Surely I have brought it forth a female
. . . . and the male is not like the female’, i.e., a daughter cannot happen to be a Rasoolas.
Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Said and Allah was more Knowing of what she gave birth to.

So when Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted Granted Isa<sup>as</sup> to Maryam<sup>as</sup>, it was so that he<sup>as</sup> was the one Imran<sup>as</sup> had been Given glad tidings with, and Promised to him<sup>as</sup>. So when we<sup>asws</sup> say something regarding the man<sup>asws</sup> from us<sup>asws</sup>, and it happens to be in his<sup>asws</sup> son, or a son of his<sup>asws</sup> son, so do not be denying that’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim his father all from ibn Mahbub from al-Ri’ab from abu Basir from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Allah sent revelation to ‘Imran saying, “I will grant you a perfect and holy son who would cure the blind and the lepers and bring the dead back to life by Allah, the permission of Allah and I make him a messenger to the israelites.”
‘Iran than told it to his wife, Hanna, mother of Mary all about it When she conceive with the baby Mary and she thought to herself that the baby will be a boy.
When she give birth to Mary she said, “Lord, I have given birth to a girl
and boys are not like girls. A girl can not be a messenger.
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious, has said, “Allah knows to who have you given birth.

When Allah, the Most High, granted Jesus to Mary he was the boy promised to ‘Imran. He promised Jesus to ‘Imran. When we would say something about a man from us and that thing would be fount in his sons or grand sons then you must not deny it.”
